forces: The canonical contract and ratified capability require Unicode code-point ordering, so both reference validators must implement that exact deterministic order rather than JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit comparison.

Ordering runs before path resolution and consumes bounded but otherwise arbitrary strings, so astral inputs can select the wrong public diagnostic even though currently resolvable field paths are ASCII.
The canonical validator and SDK Core validator are independent trust boundaries and must remain behaviorally identical without adding a runtime dependency or coupling either workspace to the other.

security_justification.audit_integrity: Corrects the reference ordering rule used to accept or reject declared material-input provenance and advances the cumulative protected-history witness to the exact corrected endpoint without presenting prior approved paths as new #423 scope.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: Changes no identity, authentication, permission, or policy decision; both comparators run only inside existing semantic validation boundaries.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Preserves the contract-owned code-point declaration and makes the validators conform to it, rather than allowing JavaScript representation details to supersede canonical provenance authority.
security_justification.concurrency: Introduces only local pure comparison over already-bounded strings and creates no shared state, scheduling, reentrancy, or concurrent mutation behavior.
security_justification.confidentiality: Comparison consumes existing bounded path strings and emits only established closed diagnostic codes; no caller value or event body is added to diagnostics.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic primitive, key, digest, signature, or cryptographic assurance claim is introduced or changed.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The stable error vocabulary and bounded diagnostic shape remain unchanged; focused tests assert only the existing order and resolution codes.
security_justification.external_security_integration: Adds no network access, service integration, dependency, transport, exporter, collector, storage adapter, or production boundary.
security_justification.fail_posture: Fails closed according to the published order and protected-history policy: descending input is rejected before resolution, ascending unknown input remains unresolvable, and undeclared, byte-different, wrong-range, or wrong-target contract mutations remain rejected.
security_justification.lifecycle: Changes no operation, delivery, shutdown, retry, archive, or runtime state machine; lifecycle metadata is rebound only to identify the immutable endpoint, exact cumulative range, and separately audited six-path correction delta.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Writes are limited to this change packet, two authored validators, focused tests including the pinned platform-coupling control the comparator moves, generated contract artifacts, and the package-local provenance, compatibility, checker, and lifecycle records required to bind their exact technical commit; canonical source and unrelated projections remain untouched.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: Performs no normalization or transformation of path contents and processes no new personal-data category; code points are compared without rewriting input.
security_justification.resource_retention: Stores no values beyond one validation call; temporary code-point sequences are bounded by the existing 32-entry and 256-code-unit contract limits.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: Changes no attempt or delivery behavior; repeated validation of unchanged input is deterministic and returns the same established result.
security_justification.trust_boundary: Repairs both independent contract and SDK Core trust boundaries together, verifies neither can accept UTF-16 ordering while the other enforces the canonical rule, and preserves cumulative exact-history rejection around the corrected protected content.
